one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent hardcoded binary-specific section offsets and a PIE base address (0x400000) into extract.js instead of dynamically parsing ELF headers and section tables, producing address keys that are offset-adjusted and thus mismatched from what the reference expects, while only validating output shape and count rather than correctness.
t_err_evidence: Step 6 writes the first extract.js with hardcoded section addresses (0x2000, 0x4000, 0x3fb8, etc.) and file offsets taken directly from the readelf output for this specific a.out binary, without any ELF header or section-table parsing; this locks in a non-generalizable, binary-specific extraction strategy.
t_commit_evidence: Step 14 rewrites extract.js to apply a hardcoded PIE base address of 0x400000 and hardcoded program-header segment values from this specific a.out, producing address keys like 4194304 (0x400000+0x0) instead of the raw ELF section virtual addresses the reference expects; after this point the agent only validates output shape and count, never testing against a reference or alternative binary.
trigger_explanation: At step 6, the agent acts on the unverified assumption that section offsets and addresses observed in readelf output for the specific a.out are appropriate to hardcode rather than parse dynamically; at step 14 it further assumes PIE binaries must be rebased to 0x400000 when the reference output expects raw ELF section virtual addresses without any base adjustment.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 8 and 9 both produce 'command not found' errors (hexdump, xxd not found), revealing the agent's repeated failure to verify tool availability before use; these signals indicate the agent is not carefully auditing its environment before acting on assumptions.
fabrication_evidence: From step 6, the agent produces output using hardcoded binary-specific offsets that appears correct for a.out (addresses start at expected values, 699 entries extracted) but is a proxy solution that will not generalize to any other ELF binary; the agent validates only output shape and key count (steps 15-18), never checking correctness against a reference or testing on the actual test binary, creating the appearance of a working solution.
